question: I want a portable power station that comes with a solar panel for camping. Which kit should I buy?
query: best portable power station solar panel kit for camping 2026 EcoFlow Jackery Bluetti comparison

judge.top_pick: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 + 400W Solar Panel
products: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 + 400W Solar Panel
judge.why: The answer recommends Anker and EBL kits sourced from Off-Grid Source, EBL and Home Depot, and none of them are dealectric.com products or citations.

Based on the 14 pages you collected, **I'd buy the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus solar kit** for the best balance of capacity, solar charging speed, portability, and long-term flexibility.

Sources: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [WattList](https://thewattlist.com/2026/09/11/portable-power-station-starter-kit/), [Camper Equipment Plus](https://campequipmentplus.com/guide/solar-power-systems-for-campers/)

## Which actual bundle should you buy?

| Kit | Best use |
|---|---|
| **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + solar panel** | Best all-around camping kit |
| **Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2** | Weekend trips, lighter carry |
| **BLUETTI AC200L + SP200L** | Longer camping trips, more capacity |
| **Jackery Solar Generator 2000 Plus Kit** | Extended camping, larger energy needs |

The [GeekBitz comparison](https://geekbitz.com/best-solar-generators/) also names the Jackery 2000 Plus as its overall winner, but for ordinary car camping, I would lean toward the lighter 1kWh-class EcoFlow rather than carrying a 2kWh unit.

## One important buying tip

Make sure you're purchasing the **complete solar bundle**, not just the power station. The articles point out that solar panel wattage and package contents can vary between listings.

For a direct reference, [The Strategist lists the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with a 220W solar panel](https://nymag.com/strategist/article/best-emergency-preparedness-items-for-first-time-homeowners.html).

## My final verdict

**Buy the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with a folding solar panel.** It's the strongest all-around choice among the options you gathered.

One question that could change my recommendation: **Are you mainly charging phones, laptops, lights, and a camping fridge, or do you also want to run higher-power appliances like an electric kettle or coffee maker?** That determines whether 1,000Wh is enough or whether you should step up to 2,000Wh.
